title: Alerts and communication
summary: A phone alert is only one way to learn what is happening.
steps: When service works, check alerts from your local emergency management agency and National Weather Service.
Wireless Emergency Alerts, radio/TV alerts, and NOAA Weather Radio may carry official warnings. Reception and coverage vary by location and equipment.
Keep a paper contact list, a battery-powered radio, and a family meeting plan. An out-of-area contact can help reconnect people.
If you cannot reach 911, look for locally announced alternatives; do not assume a nationwide backup number.
